Team —

Quick pre-brief for Alex Taylor (SWE III) who is interviewing this week. Goal: align on the role scope we expect, finalize the interviewer anchors, and lock the debrief flow so we don't have last-minute confusion. Attachments: HM_anchors_v1.pdf (anchor questions + guidance), role_scope_brief.odt (one-pager recommended scope), candidate_profile_Alex_Taylor.pdf, interview_slots.ics.

Please review HM_anchors_v1.pdf before the calibration call. Key asks:
- Confirm which of the listed focus areas are primary vs. secondary (e.g., scaling systems vs. infra observability).
- Agree on leveling signals we will use for SWE III (ownership examples, system design depth, mentoring).
- Volunteer for debrief lead (run the 15-min readout + make call on blocker signals).

Proposed debrief cadence: 10-15 minute immediate readout after last interviewer completes, then a 30-minute synced debrief if there are divergent signals. If clear hire/no-hire consensus in immediate readout, skip the long debrief.

We have a hard constraint: candidate is only available in PT mornings (8–11am PT) on Wed/Thu. I added tentative slots in interview_slots.ics and the scheduling link below.

Can you each reply with: 1) any redlines to anchors, 2) whether you can be the debrief lead, and 3) which slot you prefer?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of SWE Hiring Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks for pulling this together, Vanessa — good, pragmatic structure. A few quick notes from my side after skimming the anchors:

- Focus areas: move "service migration" from primary to secondary unless the hiring manager explicitly needs recent migration experience. For SWE III at our scale, we should emphasize ownership, incident response, and API contract design.
- Leveling: add an explicit example under "Ownership" for handling an oncall incident that crosses services (what decisions did they make; how they coordinated). That helps differentiate SWE II vs. SWE III.
- Interview runtime: recommend 45-minute deep dive + 30-minute system-design rather than two 45s; gives us time to probe end-to-end tradeoffs.

I can be debrief lead for this loop — happy to run the immediate 10–15 min readout and synthesize notes. Prefer the Wed 9am PT slot (listed in interview_slots.ics).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks — I added a short leveling rubric in the role_scope_brief.odt (page 2) with three concrete signals for SWE III:
- Ownership breadth: led a cross-team launch or owned a set of services >= 3 microservices for 6+ months.
- Technical depth: can author perf plans and tradeoffs for 2–3 scaling levers (caching, sharding, async processing).
- Mentorship: evidence of pairing/triage coaching that improved team mean time to repair.

On anchors: I agree with Marissa on the migration note. Also suggest the "Data correctness" anchor include a short live exercise: give them a small read-repair scenario to reason through (10 min). It helps separate design fluency from rote answers.

I can take the system-design slot if needed, but prefer to keep the 45/30 split that Marissa proposed (45 deep dive, 30 design). I can step in for a late swap, too — so marking myself as backup for Wed 9am PT.

Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
